metadata.title: Social Mobility and Inequality in Latin America and the Caribbean (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD report synthesises results from large-scale assessments rather than estimating a single student-level model in the report itself. It draws on PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) and PIAAC (adults 16–65) to describe proficiency distributions, socio-economic gradients (ESCS in PISA), and adult skill levels (literacy, numeracy, and PSTRE in PIAAC). Because the report presents descriptive and comparative statistics (e.g., mean scores, shares below proficiency thresholds, and differences by ESCS quartiles) without specifying an analysis pipeline with sampling/replicate weights, the report does not provide weight variable names or replicate design details for re-analysis. For any re-use of underlying microdata, analysts should apply the official complex survey design and plausible-value procedures provided by PISA/PIAAC technical documentation, but those procedures are not operationalised as a bespoke weighting strategy within this report.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable here because the report does not fit an achievement-score predictive model using PISA/PIAAC microdata; instead it reports published proficiency summaries (means, proficiency-level shares, and ESCS-related comparisons) and contextual policy interpretations. Missing-data handling is not reported because the report is a synthesis of assessment results and does not describe an original statistical estimation procedure with an explicit missing-data protocol.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report uses published results from PISA 2022 for Latin America and the Caribbean (14 LAC countries participating in PISA 2022, with some countries flagged as not meeting all sampling requirements) and published results from the first cycle of PIAAC for four LAC countries (Chile, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru). It also references additional adult-skill evidence from STEP in urban areas of Bolivia and Colombia, but does not provide an analytic microdata filtering recipe (e.g., item/module completion rules or complete-case criteria) because it is not conducting a new student-level estimation.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report synthesises evidence on social mobility and inequality in Latin America and the Caribbean using results from PISA 2022 and PIAAC (first cycle), complemented by other OECD and partner indicators. For PISA 2022, it highlights low foundational performance in mathematics, reading, and science, with Level 2 treated as the minimum proficiency benchmark and large shares of students below that threshold across LAC countries. It also reports socio-economic disparities using PISA’s ESCS index (e.g., ESCS top–bottom differences and the strength of the socio-economic gradient), interpreting these as signals of fairness and system quality rather than as causal estimates. For PIAAC, it reports adult literacy, numeracy, and problem-solving in technology-rich environments (PSTRE) proficiency distributions and links low skills to labour-market vulnerability and informality. The report does not provide an original ML modelling pipeline, performance metrics for predictive algorithms, or explicit sampling/replicate-weight handling within the report.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to ML methodology because the document is an OECD synthesis report rather than an empirical ML study with a specified modelling target, algorithmic pipeline, and reported predictive performance. It also does not provide an analytic sample definition with per-country student counts or a re-usable weighting/missing-data protocol, since it relies on published assessment outputs and descriptive comparisons. As a result, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty.
